prompt:
The snippet snippets/subscription-cadence.liquid currently fails to parse and mishandles several cases. Rewrite it to render a subscription plan's delivery cadence exactly as specified. Input. A single top-level variable is always supplied: - plan: an object, or null. When plan is an object, it always has all four of these keys: - plan.name: string or null. - plan.interval: string or null. - plan.interval_count: integer or null. It may be zero or negative. - plan.price_cents: non-negative integer or null. Rules: 1. If plan is null, output nothing. 2. Let UNIT be plan.interval stripped of surrounding whitespace and lowercased. A null value counts as an empty string. If UNIT is not exactly "day", "week", "month" or "year", output nothing. 3. Let COUNT be plan.interval_count. If it is null, or less than 1, use 1. 4. Set LABEL as follows: - When COUNT is 1, LABEL depends on UNIT: day gives Daily, week gives Weekly, month gives Monthly, year gives Yearly. - Otherwise LABEL is "Every COUNT UNITs", for example Every 2 weeks or Every 3 days. 5. Let NAME be plan.name stripped of surrounding whitespace. A null value counts as an empty string. 6. Output, in this order: -

- Only if NAME is non-empty: NAME, where NAME is HTML-escaped. - LABEL - Only if plan.price_cents is not null, a price span: - If price_cents is 0, output Free. - Otherwise output $D.CC / delivery. D is the integer number of whole dollars (price_cents divided by 100, no thousands separators). CC is the remaining cents, always two digits with zero padding. For example, 1005 becomes $10.05 and 5 becomes $0.05. -

7. The output must contain no whitespace or newlines between tags and no leading or trailing whitespace. Output only the specified elements/attributes; escape dynamic text and attributes. Inter-element whitespace, comments and quote style may vary; leaf text is exact. Change only snippets/subscription-cadence.liquid. Do not suppress checks or hardcode case values. All input keys are present.
